newsitem.title: UK: BT shareholders seek answers on MCI merger.
newsitem.headline: BT shareholders seek answers on MCI merger.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc shareholders arriving for the company's annual meeting on Wednesday said they would be seeking answers from the company on its planned merger with MCI Communications.
BT shares fell heavily last Friday after MCI issued a profits warning following larger-than-expected losses due to MCI's attempt to enter the U.S. local telephone market.

Before he went into the meeting, shareholder Alan Dobson, an Edinburgh mathematics lecturer, said: "I had faith that they (BT) had it all sewn up and knew what they were doing as regards the MCI merger."
"It is therefore all a bit of a shock to hear of the huge losses incurred in the U.S. Either BT had an inkling of this(or)if they did not they are incompetent," Dobson added.
A retired management consultant who asked not to be named, said: "I am wanting answers today. It seems to have all gone pear shaped."
Meanwhile, Tom Wilson, a retired tax inspector, said of the proposed merger: "You cannot but wonder if they have overbought."
Hilda Knowles, a retired typist said: "I only know what I have read in the newspapers, but I hope for a full explanation today from BT's chairman."
Housewife, Margaret Baillie of Edinburgh said: "There seems to be an awful lot of confusion and there appear to be too many people with a finger in the pie."
A BT spokesman said earlier on Wednesday that the company could not make any comment on MCI until after a full-scale review of its merger partner's prospects.
